description: Free UK mortgage overpayment calculator: interest and years saved by regular or lump-sum overpayments, the 10% ERC allowance and a yearly balance.

jsonld.name: UK Mortgage Overpayment Calculator
jsonld.description: Interest and time saved on a UK repayment mortgage from regular overpayments or a lump sum, with a 10% early repayment charge allowance check.

acceptedAnswer.text: Most repayment mortgages allow them, often up to a yearly percentage of the balance without an early repayment charge. Check your offer document for the cap and whether extra payments cut the term or the monthly payment.

mainEntity.name: Does this include early repayment charges?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Interest saved is amortisation only. The 10% guardrail is a typical penalty-free allowance, not your lender's ERC table.

mainEntity.name: Should I overpay or invest in an ISA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Overpaying gives a guaranteed, tax-free return equal to your mortgage rate. A stocks and shares ISA may earn more over the long run but can fall in value. Many people keep an emergency fund first, then split spare cash based on their mortgage rate and appetite for risk.

Overpaying keeps the current rate and shortens the term. Remortgaging changes the rate and usually adds fees. Use this page for extra payments and the refinance breakeven calculator if the question is a new rate.

mainEntity.name: Is this the same as the UK repayment vs interest-only calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. That page compares two products for a purchase. This page takes an existing repayment mortgage and measures the effect of overpaying.

mainEntity.name: Are these figures a lender illustration?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Confirm with your lender or a regulated adviser, especially around ERC limits.
